entityDescription:
Nicosia Municipality is the Local Authority of the Capital City of Cyprus, which is located approximately at the geographic centre of the island. Its responsibilities span the entire range of local affairs and in this capacity it cooperates with a wide array of public and private agencies. Its activities comprise development planning and development control, traffic- transportation-parking with a focus on sustainable mobility, social welfare and inclusion, energy efficiency, sustainable waste management, public health protection, culture and creativity development . 
It is the central Municipality of the greater urban area of Nicosia and Nicosia District of Nicosia accommodating approximately 40% of the population in the Government controlled area of the Republic. As the seat of the Government of the Republic of Cyprus, Nicosia hosts in its area all major institutions of the Republic and a wide range of central and district wide administrative functions and institutions with which it cooperates on a regular basis. Nicosia is also the financial and business centre of Cyprus and boasts the largest concentration of finance and business establishments. Nicosia Municipality works closely with business representative organisations (in particular with the Nicosia Chamber of Commerce and Industry) towards shared goals: to promote the city as a vibrant business centre and attract investment and development initiatives in its area and the wider city; to ensure adequate investment towards the enhancement of urban infrastructure contributing to the overall attractiveness and competitiveness of Nicosia as a destination for business, cultural, local and international tourism activities; to facilitate the organization of high caliber events etc.. In the framework of promoting its strategic goals and enhancing the opportunities for the resident population of Nicosia and its wider region, Nicosia Municipality has close relations of cooperation with the academic, research and other education and training institutions located in the wider urban area of the Capital, constituting the overwhelming majority of such institutions in Cyprus. In the same framework, it also collaborates with such institutions in other areas of Cyprus, providing leadership and acting as a catalyst in research and innovation initiatives with potential results of city- wide applicability and beyond. Not least, its strategy and action plans encompass a socially sensitive and inclusive approach, aiming to provide quality opportunities to school children and their families and to young people of great potential, including those who belong to socially vulnerable groups. Finally, Nicosia is a leading Cultural Centre in Cyprus combining a creative and high caliber human capital active in the Creative and Cultural Industry sector, but also a notable concentration of cultural infrastructure that is growing and diversifying the creative offer of the city. 
Nicosia Municipality’s integrated sustainable development strategy, taking into account the city’s and its wider region’s comparative advantages gives high priority to the development of the city as an innovation and knowledge hub. In this framework, the Municipality is joining forces with a wide range of actors and participates in partnerships and initiatives that can be catalytic towards (a) the creation and attraction of education, research, innovation establishments in its area and (b) the change of culture required at different levels, which bring closer science, innovation, entrepreneurial culture and the relevance / applicability of these in the Cypriot society and economy.

2.the Bylaw of the Central Office of Measures introduced with the Order no. 2 of the President of the Office of 28th of June 2011.
The scope of tasks of the Central Office of Measures includes issues related with scientific, legal and industrial metrology as well as hallmarking. There is a close cooperation in the above mentioned fields, which makes it easier to coordinate the execution of tasks that the Polish administration of measures is charged with.

Our Norwegian subsidiary, TestLab AS, provides arctic design services for offshore and onshore industries operating in harsh climate as well as sea route management systems for the maritime industry. We offer design, consulting, training and software solutions.

The Internet of Things is present in maritime and logistics solutions. Remote and automated monitoring. tracking, routing, warning, and control of vessels, fleet and other related assets will impact on ship, port and site operators’ costs and efficiency. Operators must carefully evaluate the types of data being communicated and the real-time requirements of such data, as to be able to offer safe and sound support of IoT for all vessels and sites concerned. Hence, our parole is to offer solutions that enable ships to be en route and sites to be in operation no matter what weather conditions they face.

TestLab works together with leading shipping companies, cruise lines, shipyards, ports, and oil companies.

entityDescription:
The decision of building the Chemical Production Plant in the woods near Jasło was made in 1937. The main task of the Plant was the production for the defensive needs of the country. However, the outbreak of World War II made it impossible to start production. Rebuild from ravages of war, the Plant started its activity in 1951 as Chemical Production Plant No 12. Among other things it produced the following: phenolic resins, granular polystyrene, laquer-grade nitrocellulose, artillery nitroglycerine powders fully satisfying needs of the army as well as exporting significant amounts of those powders. By the end of 60’s double-base propulsion charges, based on license solutions and domestic projects, were introduced for the first time into production. The 70’s brought new investments for the Plant. The special production department was enriched by the Division of Pyrotechnics, where production of pyrotechnical means for training purposes as well as smoke and illumination grenades. Propulsion charges for anti-tank rocket launchers, aircraft missiles, guided anti-tank missiles and rocket artillery were introduced into the production on a large scale. The production still covered wide assortment of artillery and mortar double-base powders.
During the 60’s and 70’s Gamrat was involved in project Meteor – meteorological rocket and was responsible for rocket propellant delivery and static fire tests. Project most advanced rocket version – Meteor 2K surpassed Institute of Aviation engineers designed maximum altitude and reached 100km commonly recognized as boundary of earth atmosphere and outer space.
In the 70’s Gamrat started extensive cooperation with civic and military scientific and research institutions. During the years which followed the technical back-up facilities were modernized, the Experimental Institute was build, the infrastructure was expanded. The Plant’s own original technologies were implemented both into civil and special production. The economic transformations that took place in Poland on the turn of the 80’s caused large decrease in number of orders from the army and following cease of research and development work. Activity of company moved to civil production. None the less by the end of 90’s new department of heterogeneous (composite) rocket propellants arisen.
The works conducted in connection with privatization of Gamrat S.A. led to establishing of the Special Production Plant “Gamrat” Ltd. (Zakład Produkcji Specjalnej “Gamrat” Sp. z o. o.) in 2003. It took over entire economical activity related to realization of military purchase orders from Gamrat S.A.. Factory was first place in Poland where composite propellants were produced at industrial scale. Recently we were engaged in project: Development of composite solid rocket propellant technology and 122mm extended range missile prototype construction and company part was to deal with implementation of short-run production of case-bonded rocket motor. Currently production of composite propellants was taken over to different entity and ZPS Gamrat field of activity narrowed to production of double-base propulsion charges and pyrotechnics. Plant stays in contact and cooperates with many R&D institutes for example: Institute of Organic Industrial Chemistry, Military Institute of Armament Technology and Institute of Aviation.

entityDescription:
The Ministry of Interior (IMI)- Department of Fire Corps, Public Rescue and Civil Defence (Ministero dell’Interno - Dipartimento dei Vigili del Fuoco, del Soccorso Pubblico e della Difesa Civile) deals with the organisation and the provision of services concerning prevention, rescue and relief activities in case of natural calamities or technological disasters. It also covers all relevant administrative and management aspects.
The Department is particularly active in two homogeneous and interconnected sectors: The Italian National Fire Corps and Civil Protection - in close cooperation with the National Civil Protection Department within the Prime Minister's Office. The Italian National Fire Corps is in charge of the protection of human life and the safeguard of property, environment from damages or potential damages caused by fire, explosion and other accidents, as well as from major industrial risks, including nuclear ones. In particular, the Italian National Fire Corps carries out the following tasks: (i) fire prevention and extinction and - in general - all emergency technical operations for the protection of human life and property; (ii) fire rescue in main national civil airports and harbours; (iii) training and deployment of units for the safeguard of civil population in case of natural disasters or war. Among these areas, the Italian National Fire Corps performs activities mainly belonging to the first point. 
To give some figures, during the year 2013 some 33.000 professionals of the Italian National Fire Corps in force in 545 HQs and Fire Stations carried out 702.112 interventions, while its prevention activity was focussed on the examination of 121.738 technical projects and the surveillance of 55.202 sites. The Italian National Fire Corps has his own fleet of 40 helicopters, 2 aeroplanes distributed over 12 bases and manages, for the needs of the forest fires activity, a fleet of 18 Canadairs.
